from._: All six out of Screen Recording 2026-09-03 194921.mp4, at 2 fps: ffmpeg -i <clip> -vf fps=2 f%04d.png

note: The MCX LT is the weapon that broke the house assumption about which slots
are on a gun and which are opened. Its upper rail and upper patch are on the
bare rifle -- the RM277 has to be given an upper rail by a barrel -- and its
LEFT AND RIGHT PATCHES are not on the rifle at all: either barrel brings
them, and the Fierce Barrel brings a heat shield as well.
What the Fierce Barrel does not do is take the muzzle. Both frames below
were cut believing it did, because neither draws a muzzle chip; the game
says otherwise. So these two arrangements are recorded a chip short rather
than re-cut from a frame nobody has, and the muzzle sits in the same
position as the killflash -- a table on the page, no chip on the stage.
Every chip in every frame is seeded by hand here rather than left to the
label reader. Two of these arrangements put three chips in a row all called
'Optic' or '...Patch' with the name clipped, and the reader cannot tell a
Left Patch from an Upper Patch from a Right Patch by its tail alone. Seeded
to the right object, snapped to the right pixel.

clips.why: The Fierce Barrel does NOT take the muzzle slot -- checked in the game after this was cut. But no muzzle chip is drawn in this frame, and there is bare screen to the left of the heat shield where one would sit, so the arrangement recorded here is one chip short of the truth. Left as watched rather than invented: the muzzle keeps its table on the page and goes without a chip on the stage until a clip catches it, the same way the killflash does.

The Fierce Barrel does NOT take the muzzle slot -- checked in the game after this was cut. But no muzzle chip is drawn in this frame, and there is bare screen to the left of the heat shield where one would sit, so the arrangement recorded here is one chip short of the truth. Left as watched rather than invented: the muzzle keeps its table on the page and goes without a chip on the stage until a clip catches it, the same way the killflash does. The riser is fitted in a slot the bare rifle already has, so this clip answers for the barrel and the riser together and for nothing else.

The modular grip's card prints Grip Mount under Conflicting Slots, so it takes that slot away as well as opening a patch. Nothing is visibly removed in this clip -- no grip was fitted to have opened a mount -- but the layout has to say what the rule says, or the page stops matching it.
